name: Proxyman
author: Proxyman LLC
summary: Debug Network Faster & Smarter with Proxyman
description: Proxyman is a high-performance Windows app, which enables developers to capture, inspect, and manipulate HTTP/HTTPS requests/responses with ease.

versions.release_notes:
✨ Features
- Headless mode: Start Proxyman with --headless to run the proxy and MCP with no window, tray icon or dialogs, so AI agents can drive it in the background. The MCP server starts it when needed with mcp-server --headless and quits it once no agent uses it. Opening Proxyman again shows the window.
- Ubuntu/Debian package: Install Proxyman from a .deb package as well as the AppImage. It installs to /opt/Proxyman with a proxyman command, and works on Ubuntu 24.04 and later without --no-sandbox or FUSE.

⚡️ Improve
- MCP: New tools to list and resume requests held at a Breakpoint, open and close session files, and create a root certificate without installing it. get_proxy_status says whether the proxy is listening, and quit_proxyman and proxyman-cli quit close Proxyman cleanly.
- MCP: Network Condition tools keep only the host and reject wildcard hosts, create_breakpoint warns when a Map Local or Block List rule stops it from pausing, and a new setup workflow fixes curl.exe's CRYPT_E_NO_REVOCATION_CHECK error on Windows.
- When a client rejects Proxyman's certificate, the connection now shows as an SSL Handshake Failed request with the likely cause and the client's error. On Windows, it explains that curl.exe needs --ssl-no-revoke.
- Linux: The update window explains how to update the way you installed Proxyman, with a copyable apt command for the .deb, and Download Update opens the new version's release page.
- Settings > Products: Redesigned, with every Proxyman platform in one row, plus Device MCP, TCP Viewer and TinyShield from the Proxyman team.
- Crash reports now go to Proxyman's own server instead of sentry.io, and still leave out your IP address, cookies and request bodies.

🐞 Bugs
- Fixed: Right-clicking a request outside the selection selects it first, so Copy, Delete, Repeat and Tools act on the request under the pointer.
- Fixed: Network Conditions throttle at the chosen speed instead of 8 times slower, an Unlimited custom bandwidth no longer hangs, and throttled requests show how long the client actually waited.
- Fixed: Editing a body at a Breakpoint only changes what you edited. Compact JSON stays compact, numbers such as large IDs stay as written, and line endings are kept.
- Fixed: Breakpoint and Compose keep repeated headers, such as Set-Cookie, in the server's order.
- Fixed: Map Local no longer adds Windows line endings to inline JSON bodies, and bodies served from a file keep their exact bytes.
- Fixed: Breakpoint, Map Local and Scripting rules created from a request only turn on SSL Proxying for https:// and wss:// URLs.
- Fixed: HAR files record afternoon times correctly instead of 12 hours early.
- Fixed: Proxyman's own update checks and crash reports no longer appear in the request list.
- Fixed: When another app uses the proxy port, Proxyman says so and how to fix it, instead of looking like the proxy is running.
- Fixed: Opening Proxyman a second time no longer disconnects MCP from the running app.
- Fixed: MCP export-log --domains matches host:port, and list_setup_workflows lists every workflow instead of the first 25.

✨ Features
- Compromised CA protection: Proxyman refuses HTTPS and WebSocket servers whose certificate chain uses one of the eMudhra intermediate CAs whose private keys leaked in October 2026, also behind an external proxy. The request is never sent, and the response, Compose, Repeat and the Connection Log say why.

⚡️ Improve
- Script Editor: Tools > Scripting on a WebSocket flow adds onWebsocket() with examples to edit, drop and send messages. The message fields, sendToClient(), sendToServer() and abort() autocomplete and explain themselves on hover, like on macOS.
- MCP: The scripting docs cover the WebSocket examples and explain that only the first matching script runs.

🐞 Bugs
- Fixed: WebSocket error messages no longer end with "undefined".

✨ Features
- Overview: See a live summary of your traffic in Capture > Overview, with charts for requests, bandwidth, status codes, top apps and domains, slow requests and errors. Copy or save it as Markdown.
- Script Templates: Start from ready-made scripts in the Scripting editor. Filter them, copy a snippet, or replace your script with one.
- WebSocket Scripting: Log, edit, drop and send WebSocket messages with onWebsocket(). Turn on Modify WebSocket Messages in the Script Editor to change them.
- Windows installer: Choose Recommended, or Custom to pick the install folder. Updates still install silently.

⚡️ Improve
- The Raw tab in Compose and Breakpoint now shows and edits the body, not only the first line and headers.
- The main table stays smooth with 100,000 requests during heavy traffic, and Auto Select keeps following the newest request.
- The Script Editor's Console Log now stays on the right, with filter, clear and hide, and shows JSON logs without escaping.
- Scripting: writeToFile() expands ~ and creates missing folders, isFileExists() is available, and JSON and form bodies are parsed whatever the case of Content-Type.
- Android Emulator setup finds system images when adb comes from Debian/Ubuntu or Google's Platform Tools, and finds Android SDKs in custom folders.
- MCP: New get_traffic_overview and list_script_templates tools, and WebSocket scripting support.

🐞 Bugs
- Fixed: The main table keeps its sort after restarting Proxyman.
- Fixed: Requests and responses held at a Breakpoint no longer fail with "socket hang up" after 30 seconds.
- Fixed: Compose and Repeat send http:// and ws:// requests without the root certificate, and no longer show an extra "Oops! Something went wrong" over the Setup Guide.
- Fixed: Proxyman asks to regenerate a root certificate from before 3.19.0 that Chrome rejects with ERR_SSL_SERVER_CERT_BAD_FORMAT, such as on PCs whose name has an underscore.
- Fixed: Proxyman can turn the Windows system proxy on and off, and restore your previous proxy on quit, when registry editing is disabled by policy. If it still can't, it shows how to set the proxy yourself.
- Fixed: Checking for updates and other Proxyman requests work on networks that inspect HTTPS with a company certificate.
- Fixed: Large requests and responses no longer hang when the disk is full.
- Fixed: When a WebSocket server disconnects abruptly, Proxyman closes the client connection too, after delivering the last messages. Binary messages from the server are no longer listed as from the client.
- Fixed: Proxyman no longer crashes when the terminal that opened it closes on Linux, when the proxy stops while a connection is opening, or when quitting stops MCP twice.
- Fixed: Turning MCP off and on quickly keeps it running.
- Fixed: Changing a checkbox in the Scripting editor no longer activates a script that wasn't saved.

✨ Features
- Apps: See which app sends each request, group traffic by app, and pin apps or enable SSL Proxying for them.
- HTTP/2: Capture and debug HTTP/2 traffic. Turn on Use HTTP/2 in Settings to get started.
- Connection Log: See connection steps, request and response headers, and errors to help find connection problems.
- Access Control: Choose which remote devices can connect to Proxyman. Allow all, block all, or allow specific IP addresses.

⚡️ Improve
- Updated proxy status and Advanced Proxy Settings to make your IP address, port, recording, and HTTP mode easier to find and change.
- Improved speed and memory use when capturing traffic, viewing Connection Logs, and working with many pinned requests.
- Added Copy Client Detection Diagnostics to the Help menu to help troubleshoot missing app names.
- JSONPath filters now explain why a filter was rejected instead of only showing no results.
- Updated Electron and other libraries to fix security issues.

🐞 Bugs
- Fixed: The cursor and text selection now line up correctly in the Scripting editor on Windows.
- Fixed: Saving a Scripting rule keeps the selected HTTP method instead of changing it to Any.
- Fixed: Scripting keeps renamed HTTP/1.1 headers, and HTTP/2 headers work correctly in custom columns and CSV exports.
- Fixed: The Client column stays visible after updating unless you choose to hide it.
- Fixed: Typing in SSL Proxying filters no longer changes selected rules, and Escape closes an open menu without closing the whole window.
- Fixed: Existing SSL Proxying rules can still be turned on or off when the free plan limit is reached.
- Fixed: Pinned requests no longer appear twice or stop updating, and deleting requests also removes them from Apps.
- Fixed: Sidebar search avoids duplicate domains and keeps matching pins and imported files visible after Clear.
- Fixed: Changing the proxy port keeps your recording and system proxy settings. Restore Default also reports when port 9090 is busy.
- Fixed: Compose correctly displays binary WebSocket messages and keeps its requests out of Remote Devices.
- Fixed: Failed WebSocket connections show the server IP when the server sends a response.
- Fixed: HTTP/2 handles large responses more reliably and retries with HTTP/1.1 when a server requires it.
- Fixed: Redacted logs and Workspace uploads remove local app paths that could reveal your computer username.
- Fixed: Log exports report write errors, saved logs keep the correct HTTP/2 version, and restored sessions avoid duplicate request IDs.

✨ Features
- Split View: View two traffic panes side by side with separate filters.
- Workspace tabs: Open traffic in separate tabs, each with its own filters and selection.
- Workspace sign-in: Sign in with a six-digit code sent to your email.
